segments.label: Paso 2 - abrir URL, iniciar sesion y permitir
segments.texto_narrado: This opens the standard *Pinterest* login screen// where the user signs in with their own account// and reviews exactly which permissions our app is requesting: *reading* and *writing* boards, and *creating* pins. Nothing happens until they tap *Allow*.

segments.label: Paso 3 - volver a terminal con tokens
segments.texto_narrado: Once the user allows access,// Pinterest redirects back to our app// and hands it a short-lived authorization code. Our script catches that code automatically// and exchanges it for an *access token* and a *refresh token*, right here in the terminal. This is the complete *authentication flow*: no passwords are ever seen or stored by our app,// only these two tokens, scoped to exactly the permissions the user approved.

segments.label: Paso 4 - cargar tokens nuevos, guardar en env
segments.texto_narrado: We save the new *access* and *refresh* tokens into our app's configuration// so every future request on behalf of this user is already authenticated.

segments.label: Paso 5 - mostrar que el token funciona
segments.texto_narrado: Now we confirm the token actually works// by asking Pinterest for the user's own boards. It *responds* with the real board list from their account,// proving the connection is live.

segments.label: Paso 6 - crear un pin real
segments.texto_narrado: Here's the *main feature* our users rely on: creating a *Pin* directly from the app. We send the image, the title, and the destination link// and Pinterest *publishes* it straight to the selected board.

segments.label: Paso 7 - confirmar pin creado
segments.texto_narrado: And *there* it is: a real Pin, live on *Pinterest*, created entirely through our app's authenticated connection// from login, to token, to a *published* Pin.
